lines: We returned with everyone breathing steadily. That is enough for me.
Home looks kinder after a dangerous road.
I am grateful we reached the walls before dark.
The journey ended without a wound to treat.
I kept the emergency bottle corked the whole way.
We chose the slower path, and it brought us home safely.
I can finally stop counting everyone behind me.
The bell sounded better than any music when we returned.
No one was lost, hurt, or left behind.
I worried often and needed none of the remedies I packed.
The road was long, but our good sense lasted longer.
I will sleep well knowing we all came back.
We reached shelter before the weather turned.
I expected trouble at every bend and found none.
You kept a steady pace when rushing would have cost us.
The village gate was the finest sight of the trip.
I returned with clean bandages and tired feet.
Safe travel does not make a grand story. I prefer it that way.
Thank you for watching the road while I watched our people.
We are home, whole, and wiser about the route.
I can tend this wound, but I wish I had not brought it home.
The road took more from me than it should have.
Give me a chair before we discuss the journey.
I kept walking after the pain started. That was not wise.
The bandage held, though barely.
Next time we turn back before someone begins bleeding.
I know how to clean this. I still resent needing to.
The village gate came into view just as my strength ran out.
I hid the limp because stopping felt more dangerous.
This bruise has a detailed opinion of our route.
I need water, clean cloth, and a night without travel.
The wound is shallow. The lesson is not.
I counted each step home after the injury.
We made it back, but I will not call that a safe journey.
My remedies were packed where I could not reach them.
Pain makes a poor traveling companion.
I should have spoken sooner when I knew something was wrong.
Let me treat this before the swelling gets worse.
I am alive and angry enough to recover.
If we go again, injury ends the trip immediately.
A wound from an enemy is simpler than one from a guide.
Following you was trust. You answered it with harm.
I will treat the injury, but not pretend it was nothing.
You were supposed to lead me home.
The road was dangerous before you turned against me.
Do not stand close while I clean what you caused.
I remember your face more clearly than the blow.
You made every step home feel unsafe.
An apology will not erase what happened out there.
I followed your directions and paid for that trust.
The body closes wounds faster than the mind does.
I will not travel with you again until this is answered.
You knew I was relying on you.
The bruise is fading. My caution around you is not.
I expected danger ahead, not beside me.
A guide who strikes you leaves no safe direction to run.
I came home alive despite your choice.
You may call it an accident when you explain it to someone else.
I need distance more than I need your help.
The journey ended at the gate. The betrayal followed me in.
The boat floated. My nerves did not.
Water carried us home, and I am grateful to be on land.
I kept the medicine dry through every wave.
The oars held, though one sounded ready to split.
I watched the shore disappear and tried not to mention it.
We reached land with all our supplies still aboard.
The crossing was calm enough for everyone except me.
I can still feel the boat rocking beneath this floor.
You chose a good landing before the weather changed.
We shared the rowing and arrived less exhausted.
A leak would have made that journey much shorter.
I counted waves until I lost track and watched you instead.
The boat was crowded, but nobody went over the side.
Next time I am packing the bottles lower in the hull.
The river current helped us more than it hindered.
I have never been so pleased to step into mud.
We tied the boat well. It should still be there tomorrow.
The spray was cold, but the route saved us hours.
I trusted your rowing after the first careful turn.
We came home by water and left our trouble on the far bank.
